An approximation to coloc using only information from fine-mapped credible sets.

Source: R/coloc-pip.R
coloc_pip.Rd

A credible set should be passed in the form of a list, data.frame, or equivalent tabular object containing at least two equal-length vectors. The object should contain at a minimim

Usage

coloc_pip(cs1, cs2, p1 = 1e-04, p2 = 1e-04, p12 = 5e-06)

Arguments

cs1

credible set 1

cs2

credible set 2

p1

prior probability a SNP is associated with trait 1, default 1e-4

p2

prior probability a SNP is associated with trait 2, default 1e-4

p12

prior probability a SNP is associated with both traits, default 1e-5

Value

a named vector containing the number of SNPs found in each credible set (nsnps1, nsnps2), the number in both credible sets (nsnps_int) and the posterior probabilities of H3 and H4 (PP.H3 and PP.H4)

Details

  • snp: a character vector of snp identifiers

  • PP: a numeric vector of posterior probabilities

Each cs may additionally contain a column

  • beta: the estimated per all snp effect on the trait

If they both do, then the returned object will also include "freq_sign_agree", which is the proportion of snps in both credible sets for which the difrection of effects (sign of beta) agrees. This is a useful quantity to be able to say "higher gene expression associates with higher (lower) disease risk" when freq_sign_agree=1 (0). If 0 < freq_sign_agree < 1 then there is some disagreement between SNPs and users are invited to investigate potential causes of this further.

Author

Jeffrey Pullin, Chris Wallace

Examples

cs1 <- data.frame(snp=c("s1","s2"), PP=c(0.05,0.9))
cs2 <- data.frame(snp=c("s1","s2","s3"), PP=c(0.1,0.8,0.05))
coloc_pip(cs1,cs2)
#>          nsnps1          nsnps2       nsnps_int           PP.H3           PP.H4 
#>    2.0000000000    3.0000000000    2.0000000000    0.0004894155    0.9995105845 
#> freq_sign_agree 
#>              NA
